audit.why: 52.82% over 3374 games — the largest sample in my slice — at EVEN 6/10 with carry threat 8.5/10. Correct: Riven wins the lane, Sylas wins the game if the lane does not close it.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] tells the player 'Your Q cooldown reduction from levels keeps short-trades in your favour'. Broken Wings has a FLAT 13-second cooldown at every rank in the kit file — there is no rank scaling on her Q at all.
audit.why: The scaling that actually exists is on the other two: Ki Burst 11/10/9/8/7 and Valor 10/9/8/7/6. The advice is right for the wrong reason, which means a player who ranks Q chasing a cooldown that never shrinks gets the opposite of what the page promised.
audit.corrected: whys[3] restated on the abilities that really scale.

audit.why: The core read is right and rare: W stun interrupting Abscond strands a champion whose whole kit is re-positioning. Chain Lash at 775 range with a delayed detonation at the intersection, Kingslayer as a 400-range healing lunge, and Abscond's recast pulling HIM to you are all represented accurately in the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built on 'track Abscond / Abduct' and 'track his E cooldown' without ever printing a number, and the level-6 section discusses trading ultimates without either ultimate's cooldown.
audit.why: Abscond is 13/12/11/10/9s — at rank 1 it is longer than your Ki Burst, which is what makes the level-2 and level-3 all-ins real. And Hijack is 80/55/30 against your Blade of the Exile at 120/90/60: he gets his ultimate back FIRST, every time, at every rank. The page's advice to bait the steal and re-engage is correct, but a player who thinks ultimates trade one-for-one here will bait it a second time and find he already has another.
audit.corrected: Abscond's 13s added to whys[0]; the 80-vs-120 gap written into content.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The flagged needs-antiheal interaction never reaches the content layer. Kingslayer heals him against champions on a cooldown that drops to 6 seconds, and Grievous Wounds appears only in one encoding-damaged report line.
audit.why: whys[3], whys[6], spikes[0] and late all describe his healing as the thing that beats you, and none of them names the item that answers it.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into content.mid alongside the W cooldown.

audit.why: The packet suspectName on wants.you[2] ('Use Blade') is a FALSE POSITIVE — the string is 'Use Blade of the Exile R1 early', Riven's real R. No rename made.

edits.before: Sylas has no dash at level 1 — he can only poke with Chain Lash outer ring. Farm safely and track his E cooldown before stepping up.
edits.after: Sylas has no dash at level 1 — only Chain Lash's outer ring pokes. Abscond arrives at 2 on a 13-second cooldown; start counting it from there.

edits.before: Your Q cooldown reduction from levels keeps short-trades in your favour — poke him down between W cooldowns and never let Kingslayer top him back up.
edits.after: Broken Wings stays 13 seconds at every rank, but Ki Burst falls to 7 and Valor to 6 — rank those and short trades tilt further your way each level.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain your window — keep wave pressure and force short trades where your Q resets proc Runic Blade autos faster than his sustain can undo them. At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Sylas steals Wind Slash with his R and it is genuinely dangerous, so never throw your second-cast execute as the opener. Instead, pop Blade of the Exile R1 to trigger the steal window, let him waste the stolen slash or let it expire, then re-engage — his stolen R has a short use-window and he will often panic-cast it early. Once the stolen slash is gone you have your full damage advantage back and he has nothing. Force the all-in in that gap.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 remain your window — force short trades where your Q resets proc Runic Blade autos faster than Kingslayer can undo them, and buy Grievous Wounds, because that heal comes back every 12 seconds and eventually every 6. At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Hijack is 80 seconds at rank 1 against your 120, so he gets his ultimate back first and you never trade them evenly. Never open with your second-cast execute. Pop Blade of the Exile R1 to trigger the steal, let him waste or expire the stolen slash, then re-engage — once it is gone your damage advantage is back and he has nothing. Force the all-in in that gap.

notes: One thing I could not settle from the kits: the page calls Abscond / Abduct a 'dash + stun (recast pull)' in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t. Riot's E text here says only 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — no stun, and the kit carries no hardCC flag on E. Per the rule that an empty flag means UNKNOWN rather than 'no', I did NOT remove the stun claim, but the player is being told to fear a stun the data does not confirm and the recast pulls HIM to her, not her to him. Recorded in unverified — a wiki check would settle it and it affects three strings.
